# DevDeskApp Documentation (llms-full.txt)

> Machine-readable reference for AI agents, LLM tool calling and automation engineers.
> Canonical URL: https://docs.devdeskapp.com/llms-full.txt
> Documentation: https://docs.devdeskapp.com
> Web application: https://www.devdeskapp.com
> npm package: https://www.npmjs.com/package/n8n-nodes-devdeskapp
> Template #21017: https://n8n.io/workflows/21017-format-json-and-secure-hr-payloads-with-devdeskapp-utilities/

---

## 1. Summary

DevDeskApp has two parts:
1. **Web app**: 340+ browser-based developer tools (formatters, encoders, hash generators, generators, CTC and HR calculators) at https://www.devdeskapp.com. Tools process input in the browser.
2. **n8n community node** `n8n-nodes-devdeskapp` (v0.1.6, MIT): one node, "DevDeskApp", with **19 operations in 5 resources**.

Node behaviour:
- Runs synchronously inside the n8n process. No external API calls and no credentials.
- Every output item carries `pairedItem: { item: i }`.
- Errors throw `NodeOperationError` linked to the item. If the node's **On Error** setting is set to continue, failed items return `{ "error": "<message>" }`.
- `usableAsTool: true`: it can be attached to an n8n AI Agent's Tool port.
- Measured node logic (10,000 items, compiled v0.1.6, Node.js 24): CTC 12.6 ms, prettify 22.6 ms, slugify 40.7 ms, SHA-256 46.5 ms. That is about 0.001 to 0.005 ms per item, before n8n's own overhead.

---

## 2. Operations reference

Parameter names are the internal n8n names. JSON operations read `jsonInput`, Crypto operations read `textPayload`, and Text operations read `textInput`.

### 2.1 JSON (`json`)

| Operation | Parameters | Output |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `prettify` | `jsonInput`, `indentation` (`2` default, `4`, `tab`) | `formatted`, `success`. Throws on invalid JSON. |
| `minify` | `jsonInput` | `minified`, `success`. Throws on invalid JSON. |
| `validate` | `jsonInput` | `valid`, plus `parsed` (valid) or `error` (invalid). Never throws. |

Prettify, input `{"service":"payment","status":"success","empId":1042}`:
```json
{ "formatted": "{\n  \"service\": \"payment\",\n  \"status\": \"success\",\n  \"empId\": 1042\n}", "success": true }
```

Validate, input `{"service": payment}`:
```json
{ "valid": false, "error": "Unexpected token 'p', \"{\"service\": payment}\" is not valid JSON" }
```

### 2.2 Crypto (`crypto`)

| Operation | Parameters | Output |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `hash` | `textPayload`, `hashAlgorithm` (`md5`, `sha1`, `sha256` default, `sha512`) | `algorithm`, `input`, `hash` (hex) |
| `base64Encode` | `textPayload` | `encoded`, `original` |
| `base64Decode` | `textPayload` | `decoded`, `original` |
| `uuid` | none | `uuid`, `version` (4) |

Hash, input `devdeskapp_production_webhook_secret_key`, sha256:
```json
{
  "algorithm": "sha256",
  "input": "devdeskapp_production_webhook_secret_key",
  "hash": "7ac4c84d335afd794bde94eb049d2259cc348357a96538929f263f7c5911a686"
}
```

Base64 encode, input `devdeskapp-secure-automation`:
```json
{ "encoded": "ZGV2ZGVza2FwcC1zZWN1cmUtYXV0b21hdGlvbg==", "original": "devdeskapp-secure-automation" }
```

UUID:
```json
{ "uuid": "8af08c51-e5bf-4800-85a4-0ec7f7f24eea", "version": 4 }
```

A plain hash is not a signature. Use `ecommerce.webhookVerifier` to verify HMAC webhook signatures.

### 2.3 Text (`text`)

| Operation | Parameters | Output |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `slugify` | `textInput` | `original`, `slug` |
| `caseConverter` | `textInput`, `targetCase`: `camelCase`, `kebabCase` (default), `lowerCase`, `pascalCase`, `snakeCase`, `upperCase` | `original`, `casing`, `result` |
| `urlEncode` | `textInput` | `original`, `encoded`, `success` |
| `urlDecode` | `textInput` | `original`, `decoded`, `success` (plus `error` if malformed) |

Only the six `targetCase` values above work. Other values (for example `lower` or `title`) return `"result": ""` without an error. There is no `convertedText` field.

Slugify, input `DevDeskApp: High-Performance Node & AI Utilities 2026!`:
```json
{ "original": "DevDeskApp: High-Performance Node & AI Utilities 2026!", "slug": "devdeskapp-high-performance-node-ai-utilities-2026" }
```

Case converter, input `Employee Salary Record`, snakeCase:
```json
{ "original": "Employee Salary Record", "casing": "snakeCase", "result": "employee_salary_record" }
```

URL encode, input `developer tools & n8n`:
```json
{ "original": "developer tools & n8n", "encoded": "developer%20tools%20%26%20n8n", "success": true }
```

### 2.4 Calculator (`calculator`)

`ctcToInHand`: parameters `annualCtc` (default 1200000) and `basicPercentage` (default 50).

Formula:
- Monthly basic = annual CTC × basic % ÷ 12.
- Employee PF = employer PF = min(12% of monthly basic, ₹1,800).
- Monthly gross = (annual CTC − 12 × employer PF) ÷ 12.
- Professional tax = ₹200 per month.
- TDS = new-regime slabs on (12 × gross − ₹75,000 standard deduction), divided by 12.
- In-hand = gross − employee PF − PT − TDS.

It does not model HRA, special allowance, the old regime, ESIC, cess, surcharge or rebates. Treat results as estimates.

Output for `annualCtc: 2400000`, `basicPercentage: 50`:
```json
{
  "annualCtc": 2400000,
  "monthlyGross": 198200,
  "monthlyInHand": 163075,
  "breakdown": {
    "monthlyBasic": 100000,
    "employeePf": 1800,
    "employerPf": 1800,
    "professionalTax": 200,
    "estimatedMonthlyTds": 33125
  },
  "taxRegime": "India Standard / New Tax Benchmark",
  "reference": "https://www.devdeskapp.com/ctc-to-in-hand-calculator"
}
```

Other CTCs (monthly gross / TDS / in-hand): ₹12L 98,200 / 6,563 / 89,638 · ₹18L 1,48,200 / 18,125 / 1,28,075 · ₹21L 1,73,200 / 25,625 / 1,45,575 · ₹28L 2,31,533 / 43,125 / 1,86,408.

### 2.5 E-commerce & FinTech (`ecommerce`)

| Operation | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- |
| `catalogMapper` | Map product catalogs between Shopify, WooCommerce and Google Merchant Center |
| `upiQr` | Build a UPI payment URI and QR payload |
| `gstJsonToTable` | Flatten GSTR-1, GSTR-3B or GSTR-2B JSON into table rows |
| `profitCalculator` | Profit margin and ROAS after commission, shipping, ad spend and RTO |
| `shippingLabelCrop` | Crop coordinates for carrier shipping labels on A4 or thermal pages |
| `webhookVerifier` | Verify Razorpay, Shopify, Stripe or custom HMAC-SHA256 webhook signatures |
| `whatsappPayload` | Build WhatsApp interactive message payloads |

Full parameters: https://docs.devdeskapp.com/n8n/operations

---

## 3. Installation

### n8n UI (recommended)
1. **Settings → Community Nodes → Install**.
2. Enter `n8n-nodes-devdeskapp`.
3. Tick the risk acknowledgement and click **Install**.

### Docker
```bash
docker exec -it n8n sh -c "mkdir -p ~/.n8n/nodes && cd ~/.n8n/nodes && npm install n8n-nodes-devdeskapp"
docker restart n8n
```

### Manual (self-hosted)
```bash
mkdir -p ~/.n8n/nodes && cd ~/.n8n/nodes
npm install n8n-nodes-devdeskapp
# restart n8n
```

In queue mode, install the package on the main instance and every worker. To use the node as an AI Agent tool on self-hosted n8n, set `N8N_COMMUNITY_PACKAGES_ALLOW_TOOL_USAGE=true`.

Fixes after import (as of 4 Nov 2026):
- 21593: fix the sample Code node string. Hash `$('DevDeskApp: JSON Prettifier & Schema Validator').item.json.formatted`. Read `prettified.formatted`, not `prettified.prettified`.
- 21594: read `salary.breakdown.monthlyBasic`, `salary.breakdown.employeePf` and `salary.breakdown.professionalTax`.
- 21595: set `targetCase` to `lowerCase`, and hash `{{ $json.result }}`.
- 21596: hash `$('Sample Notion Article Draft').item.json.rawHtmlContent`. Use `article.articleTitle` for the post title (there is no Title Case option).

Import: open the template on n8n.io and click **Use for free**, or copy the workflow JSON and paste it onto an n8n canvas with Ctrl+V / Cmd+V.

---

## 5. AI Agent tool usage

1. Add an **AI Agent** node and connect a chat model.
2. Click **+** on the agent's **Tool** input and add **DevDeskApp**. Use one resource and operation per tool node.
3. Fill model-supplied values with `$fromAI()`, for example `{{ $fromAI('annualCtc', 'Annual CTC in rupees', 'number') }}`.

Suggested system prompt:
```markdown
You can call DevDeskApp tools.
- For any salary, PF, professional tax or take-home question, call the CTC tool. Never calculate it yourself.
- For hashes, Base64 or UUIDs, call the matching DevDeskApp tool and return its exact output.
- Quote numbers exactly as the tool returns them.
```

Data sent to the chat model goes to that model's provider. Hash or strip sensitive fields before they reach the agent.
